title: Principle Intelligence and Open Structural Learning: From Sparse Differential Evidence to Open-LHS Principles, Two-Way Validation, and Portable Intelligence
description: Principle Intelligence and Open Structural Learning develops a structural learning framework in which reusable Principles can be extracted from sparse and differential evidence, validated through supporting evidence, counter-evidence, and Two-Way CCC, and evolved as evidence-bound Knowledge Roots. The framework introduces the Open-LHS Principle: the left-hand side of a Principle is not restricted to a permanently predefined symbolic vocabulary. Existing, retrieved, composed, or runtime-generated intelligence structures—including observations, differences, metrics, trajectories, CCCs, Principles, counter-evidence, triggers, policies, PIRPs, PIRUs, and other typed structural objects—may participate in Principle formation and evaluation. When required structure is missing, Runtime Structural Generation may search, retrieve, compose, generate, unfold, or delegate the creation of a compatible structure and bind it into active reasoning. The repository connects Principle Intelligence with Differential Intelligence, Context-Condition-Consequence structures, Two-Way validation, Counter-Evidence Delta Intelligence, Knowledge Root Systems, Universal Typing and Naming, Portable Intelligence Runtime Pieces and Units, Collective Structural Learning, and Open-Ended Structural Growth. Its central research proposition is that reusable intelligence structures can sometimes be extracted from experience, preserved with evidence and provenance, revised through counter-evidence, externalized for portable reuse, and incorporated into an extensible structural vocabulary for future intelligence.
notes: Version 1.0.0 is the initial research release of Principle Intelligence and Open Structural Learning. The release focuses on conceptual architecture, research vocabulary, eight core research papers, three canonical cases, seven architecture figures, Principle lifecycle design, Open-LHS, Runtime Structural Generation, Counter-Evidence, Knowledge Roots, PIRP/PIRU integration, Collective Structural Learning, and a future experimental roadmap. It intentionally does not claim a complete Principle Engine, universal ontology, universal formal logic, or production-scale collective intelligence runtime.
